item.question: Construct a rectangle where one of its sides is 5 cm and the length of a diagonal is 7 cm.
steps_tex: Draw base $DC = 5\text{ cm}$.
At $C$ draw a line $l$ perpendicular to $DC$ (that is, $90^\circ$).
With the compass opened to $7\text{ cm}$ and centre $D$, draw an arc that cuts line $l$. The cutting point is $B$ (where $DB = 7\text{ cm}$).
Draw a perpendicular to $DC$ at $D$ and a perpendicular to $BC$ at $B$. They meet at $A$. (Or use the compass to mark $A$ so that $DA = CB$ and $AB = DC$.)
Check: $AB = 5\text{ cm}$, $BC = AD$, angles $90^\circ$, diagonal $DB = 7\text{ cm}$.
item.answer_tex: Rectangle $ABCD$ with $DC = AB = 5\text{ cm}$ and diagonal $DB = 7\text{ cm}$. The other two sides $AD = BC$ come out about $4.9\text{ cm}$ and all four angles are $90^\circ$.
steps: Draw base DC = 5 cm.
At C draw a line l perpendicular to DC (that is, 90°).
With the compass opened to 7 cm and centre D, draw an arc that cuts line l. The cutting point is B (where DB = 7 cm).
Draw a perpendicular to DC at D and a perpendicular to BC at B. They meet at A. (Or use the compass to mark A so that DA = CB and AB = DC.)
Check: AB = 5 cm, BC = AD, angles 90°, diagonal DB = 7 cm.
item.answer: Rectangle ABCD with DC = AB = 5 cm and diagonal DB = 7 cm. The other two sides AD = BC come out about 4.9 cm and all four angles are 90°.

topic_name: Points the Same Distance from Two Points

item.question: The two circles of radius 5 cm centred at B and at C meet at a point (the apex A). How far is that point from B? How far is it from C? a) Distance from B b) Distance from C
steps: The point lies on the circle centred at B with radius 5 cm.
So it is 5 cm from B.
It also lies on the circle centred at C with radius 5 cm, so it is 5 cm from C.
This is the apex A.
item.answer: a) 5 cm, b) 5 cm. So it is the point A.
item.text:

2. So it is 5 cm from B.
3. It also lies on the circle centred at C with radius 5 cm, so it is 5 cm from C.
4. This is the apex A.
Answer: a) 5 cm, b) 5 cm. So it is the point A.

item.question: Was it necessary to draw two full circles to get the point A?
steps: The point A is where the two circles cross.
Only the small parts near the crossing matter.
Draw just arcs from B and from C with 5 cm radius.
Where they cross is A.
item.answer: No. Only a part of each circle is needed, so short arcs of radius 5 cm from B and from C that cross at A are enough.

steps_tex: Person: draw a circle with the compass for the head, then a neck line and a square for the body.
Wave: mark equal parts on a central line and draw half circles with the compass, one above and the next below.

Eyes: draw a light horizontal line. From a point $A$ (above it) draw the lower curve, and from a point $B$ (below it) draw the upper curve, with the same compass opening, so the two arcs meet at the ends.
Place $A$ and $B$ symmetrically (same distance from the line) so the eye is symmetrical.
Copy the eye for the second one and add the pupils.
item.answer_tex: Open drawing. item.question: Is there a 4-sided figure in which all the sides are equal in length but is not a square? If such a figure exists, can you construct it? a) Does such a figure exist? b) Can you construct it?
steps_tex: Take side length $5\text{ cm}$. Draw $AB = 5\text{ cm}$ and $AC = 5\text{ cm}$ with angle $A$, not equal to $90^\circ$, for example $60^\circ$.
The fourth point $D$ must be $5\text{ cm}$ from both $B$ and $C$.
With the compass at $5\text{ cm}$, draw an arc from $B$ and an arc from $C$. They cross at $D$.
Join $BD$ and $CD$. All four sides $AB$, $AC$, $BD$, $CD$ are $5\text{ cm}$.
The angles are not $90^\circ$, so it is not a square.
item.answer_tex: $(a)$: Yes, a rhombus (diamond) with four equal sides and angles that are not $90^\circ$; $(b)$: yes, it can be constructed with compass arcs.
steps: Take side length 5 cm. Draw AB = 5 cm and AC = 5 cm with angle A, not equal to 90°, for example 60°.

Join BD and CD. All four sides AB, AC, BD, CD are 5 cm.
The angles are not 90°, so it is not a square.
item.answer: a) Yes, a rhombus (diamond) with four equal sides and angles that are not 90°; b) yes, it can be constructed with compass arcs.
